analysis:
Integration pass over the full PR: the workflow change (.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml), a changelog entry, docs (docs/developer/build.md, docs/developer/test.md) and the CI test script (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py). No provider runtime, wire protocol, attestation, key custody, cache (T-041) or fan-helper code changes, so A-001..A-020 and TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012/013/014 are unaffected.

Verified the router patch directly. It adds the header X-Darkbloom-Run-Scoped-Labels: 1 (no secret, body unchanged). The jq expression now appends -run-<RUN_ID> to the last profile label, after any size suffix. RUN_ID is passed via --arg as a string, so there is no injection path. The existing exact-match check against the profile array, the fork-PR guard, the https-only restriction, the size and time limits and the plane-text sanitizer are unchanged. A generic, other-run or extended label set therefore falls back to the Blacksmith runner. This tightens CI runner selection so an idle runner from an older run cannot take a newer run's job.

Tests (scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py) pin the header, the exact current-run labels for both profiles with and without sizes, the fallback for legacy, other-run and extra-label grants, and that two runs get incompatible label sets. Docs and the changelog match the code.

Limits: the integration source is incomplete (33 units omitted), but the patches seen are complete for the workflow, tests and docs. Whether the external routing plane and its runners honor run-scoped labels is platform-owned and unverified. A mismatch would degrade to the fallback runner (availability and cost), not a security regression. CI routing sits outside the provider threat model's scope. No findings and no threat-model update needed.
